title: Hruday boundary comparison of the Heisenberg dynamics of the named constructions on compact windows
selection_reason: Deliberation loop 1: a Duhamel sum over the extra F2 faces with the AQ1 Nachtergaele-Sims constants gives an explicit O(N^-2) comparison of the two families' Heisenberg dynamics on compact windows (modern and skeptic previews 2.566e-11 and 2.549e-11 times (5N+1)/N^3 at |theta|=8). It addresses AY2 obligations O5 and O6 and is independent of BA1.
model: Zero-selected patterned family (AM2/AQ1) as in BA1, both signs |tau|<=10^-8; construction families F1 (AQ1 centered whole-star boxes) and F2 (I1 section 6 all-contained-face boxes with padding) on the same Lambda_N, N>=2; Heisenberg dynamics generated by the finite-box Hamiltonians with the unbounded on-site Casimir terms h_b and bounded finite-range interactions; observables A in B(H_R), cover R={0,e_z}.

parameters.metric: l1 metric on Z^3 fine sites as in AQ1 (F(r)=(1+r)^-4, convolution constant C<=224, ||Phi||_F<=2268|tau|); F2 owner-set interaction ||Phi'||_F<=1323|tau| (AY1 reverse); the coarse-to-fine distance conversion stated
parameters.weights: Lieb-Robinson decay function F(r)=(1+r)^-4 (polynomial, AQ1); an exponential F_mu(r)=e^{-mu r}F(r) is a separately labelled instance with its own constants and is optional
parameters.window: |theta|<=8 in theta=alpha t/hbar (normalized u=theta/8<=1 internally); compact window only, no uniform-in-time claim
parameters.boundary_source: the 28N(5N+1) faces present in F2 and not in F1 on Lambda_N, at l1 distance at least N-1 from R (coarse), to be derived by enumeration plus an all-size argument

targets.comparison: ||tau^{F2,N}_theta(A)-tau^{F1,N}_theta(A)|| <= 6x10^-11 (5N+1) N^-3 ||A|| for |theta|<=8, N>=2 (polynomial_lieb_robinson tier; previews 2.549e-11 and 2.566e-11)
targets.within_family_cauchy: ||tau^{F1,N+1}_theta(A)-tau^{F1,N}_theta(A)|| <= 2.5x10^-10/(N-1) ||A|| for |theta|<=8, N>=2 (preview 1.0195e-10); the O(1/N) rate is the honest polynomial-F rate
targets.f2_dynamics: the F2 finite-box evolutions converge in norm on compact windows and their limit equals the AQ1 F1 limit dynamics T_theta

required: 1. Quote the Lieb-Robinson inequality verbatim as the AQ1 report states it (Nachtergaele-Sims arXiv:1410.8174v1 Section 3 / Theorem 4.1, as cited there), with F, C and ||Phi||_F named, and place the unbounded on-site terms h_b in the interaction picture exactly as that theorem requires; never paraphrase it.

2. Derive the F2-minus-F1 boundary source on Lambda_N: the extra faces, their count 28N(5N+1), their anchors and their exact l1 distance (at least N-1 in coarse units, converted to fine units) from R, by enumeration on Lambda_2 and Lambda_3 plus an all-size argument; charge each face exactly once.

3. Prove the Duhamel comparison ||tau^{F2,N}_theta(A)-tau^{F1,N}_theta(A)|| <= B(N)||A|| for |theta|<=8 with B(N) explicit, quadratic in tau (state why the first order vanishes or is bounded), with the inner-family constants of the family whose evolution is inside the integral named; evaluate at the cap, both signs, and meet the frozen target 6x10^-11 (5N+1) N^-3 (margin at least 2).

4. Prove the within-family Cauchy estimate for F1 (and the same for F2) at the honest polynomial rate and meet 2.5x10^-10/(N-1); prove that the F2 evolutions converge on compact windows and that the limit equals the AQ1 limit dynamics; never claim exponential decay in N with the polynomial F.

5. State the honest meaning: algebraic Heisenberg dynamics of the named constructions on a compact window; not equality of GNS dynamics or of correlation functions of different states (those need BB2); export the gate fields; quote the mandatory sentence template once as one unbroken span.

6. Declare and check the tau -> tau/100 scaling of each headline constant (quadratic comparison: bracket [9900,10100]; Cauchy estimate: linear or quadratic as derived, bracket declared before evaluation); exact finite fixtures for the traps (polynomial versus exponential tail; an unbounded on-site term placed wrongly; an inner-family constant swapped); every control executed as a damaging mutation.
claim_exclusions: equality of GNS dynamics or of correlation functions of different states
exponential decay in N with the polynomial Lieb-Robinson function
uniqueness of every infinite-volume ground state
any estimate uniform in the lattice spacing a
direction_note: Forward: Duhamel over the extra F2 faces with the inner F1 evolution bounded by the AQ1 Nachtergaele-Sims constants. Reverse: each family against its own Nachtergaele-Sims limit (Phi: 2268|tau|; owner-set Phi': 1323|tau|) plus proof that the two limits coincide, then the comparison bound by the triangle inequality with its own constants. Independence is limited to route and code.

acceptance.accepted_within_scope: Both routes prove the comparison and the within-family Cauchy estimate with the frozen targets met (margin at least 2) and the F2 limit dynamics identified with AQ1's.
acceptance.limited: Only the comparison or only the Cauchy estimate is proved, or a target is met only with margin below 2.
acceptance.insufficient: The Lieb-Robinson inequality does not apply to the unbounded on-site terms as placed, or the boundary source is miscounted.

preregistration.state_provenance: finite-box Heisenberg dynamics of the named construction families F1 and F2 (no state provenance: operator-norm comparison)
preregistration.error_terms_rule: an entry may be not_applicable only with a stated reason

target.quantity: comparison coefficient and Cauchy coefficient at |theta|<=8
target.note: blind discriminating threshold for a new estimate; deliberation previews 2.549e-11/2.566e-11 and 1.0195e-10 give margins of about 2.3 and 2.45

preregistration.mandatory_sentence_template: For the zero-selected patterned family at the same coupling |tau|<=10^-8 and every A in B(H_R) with ||A||<=1 on the fixed cover R, the finite-box Heisenberg evolutions of the named construction families F1 and F2 on the same centered coarse cube Lambda_N satisfy ||tau^{F2,N}_theta(A)-tau^{F1,N}_theta(A)|| <= B(N) for |theta|<=8 in the common clock theta=alpha t/hbar; this is an algebraic comparison of the dynamics of the named constructions on a compact time window at a rate in N, not equality of GNS dynamics or of correlation functions of different states, not a uniform-in-time statement, and not a statement uniform in the lattice spacing a.
forbidden_phrasings: uniqueness of the infinite-volume ground state

scaling_brackets_per_constant.cauchy_coefficient: declared by the producer before evaluation from the derived tau order; [99,101] if linear, [9900,10100] if quadratic
